findings.title: Load tests are outside the load tier and have no CI gate step
findings.description: Task 33 (line 276) calls its 200-pair, hung-dispatcher test a "network-layer load test", and Task 24 (line 223) calls its eight-way concurrency test a load test. Both are in `tests/benchmark/`, not `tests/load/`, and no task confirms CI gates them. The load-tier rule requires network, concurrency and environment-layer paths to have a `tests/load/` test that CI gates. Sibling slice 424 does this with an explicit confirm step (`424-tasks.producer-only-replay-runner.md:128`). CI runs a bare `uv run pytest` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:38`), so these tests would still execute, but they should move to `tests/load/` with the confirm step added.

findings.title: The environment load test asserts isolation, not a bound
findings.description: Task 24's concurrency test checks distinct scrubbed homes, no shared branch and no shared registry path. Those are functional checks. The load-tier rule says load tests assert latency, throughput or resource bounds. Add a bound, such as a wall-time limit for eight concurrent `invoke` calls, and keep the isolation assertions alongside it.

findings.title: Task 8's gate contradicts the context summary on renamed names
findings.description: The context summary (line 39) says that if a 421–425 name differs, use the real one and record it in the DEVLOG. Task 8 says any missing name writes `BLOCKED:`. A renamed but present class would block under Task 8 and pass under line 39. Task 8 should state both cases: absent under any name means BLOCKED; present under another name means use it and record the mapping.

findings.title: Nothing refreshes the slice branch from the target after the gate
findings.description: Tasks 2–7 are committed on the slice branch, which is cut before 421–425 exist. When the gate clears, Task 9 onward needs those modules, but no step refreshes the branch from the target. The likeliest conflict is Task 5: line 98 says 421, 422 and 425 add keys to the same `config/keys.py`. Add a step after the gate: refresh the slice branch from the target if it merges cleanly; if it conflicts, abort and ask the Project Manager.

findings.title: The breakdown is overweight: 42 top-level tasks in one 343-line file
findings.description:
Several groups of tasks change one module under one commit, so they split work without splitting risk. Merge candidates:
- Tasks 15–19 (five stages of `qualify_slice_candidate`, one commit at line 193): merge 16+17 (sandboxes, sets, repeats) and 18+19 (case, errors) for three tasks.
- Tasks 31–34 (four tasks in `diff_judge_runner.py`): merge 31+32 (plan) and 33+34 (bound, cap, lock, resume).
- Task 40 (slash-command doc lines plus a sync test): fold into Task 35.
- Task 6 is too large for one step. Its ten synthetic builders and the live `real_landings.json` capture (line 107) are different kinds of work. Split the live capture into its own task.

findings.title: Task 6 does not say which squadron slices to record
findings.description: "Squadron's 400-initiative slices" names no indices. A junior AI has to choose them, and the choice decides whether a two-parent and a fast-forward landing exist. Name the indices or state the selection rule.

findings.title: Task 1's commit subject is over the length guideline
findings.description: `docs: correct slice 426 design for judge_pair counting, fork plan files, registration branch, keep and over-size counts` is about 118 characters against the roughly 72-character guideline. Shorten the subject, for example `docs: correct slice 426 design gaps`, and put the detail in the body.

findings.title: Task 11's file placement conflicts with the design
findings.description: The design places `SliceCandidateRejection` in `benchmark_models.py` (`426-slice.slice-cases.md:321`). Task 11 allows a split into `metrology/slice_case_models.py` if the file would pass about 300 lines, and the context summary calls it "the slice models module". Pick one location now, or have the design name the split file.

findings.title: Task 8's precondition list omits CLI flags the live tasks depend on
findings.description: Tasks 23, 26 and 41 use `--max-cost-per-replay`, `--case`, `replay-show --diff`, `auth-check` and `--review-cost`. These appear in the 424 and 425 task files, so they are planned. Task 8 checks names only, so a flag missing at build time would surface during a live run. Add the flags to the gate's check.

findings.title: Sandbox coverage relies on 421's load test, which has no CI gate step
findings.description: The context summary (line 53) says sandbox and install paths are covered by 421's load test. 421 adds `tests/load/test_benchmark_sandbox_concurrency.py` but has no confirm-CI step, unlike 424. That coverage holds only if the test is actually gated in CI.

findings.title: The design's frontmatter omits two prerequisites
findings.description: `dependencies` lists 421, 422, 424 and 425. The design's Prerequisites also name 403 and 177. The task file's frontmatter lists all six, so only the design needs the fix.

findings.title: Every success criterion has a task
findings.description: I checked the functional, technical and integration criteria against the tasks: rejections (13, 14, 15, 18), qualified case fields (14, 16–18), cf-registered runner with an unchanged user registry (24, 26), normalization on a real slice diff (7), over-size and absence handling (27, 29, 31), bound and cap (33), reports and pairwise (36–38), the mixed-kind run (39), and yield rows (22). No criterion lacks a task.

findings.title: Test tasks follow their implementation tasks
findings.description: Each implementation task is followed by its own test task, and the assertions match the design's contracts. The existing suites that must pass unchanged (`tests/replay/`, the 421 store tests, the 424 drop tests) are named in the success lines.

findings.title: Failure modes each have an observable-signal test
findings.description: The context summary lists seven failure modes, and each maps to a test that asserts an ERROR or WARNING log plus a recorded outcome: git failure (13), cf step (4, 24), judge hang and failure (3, 30, 33), missing tip sha (31), store write (12, 34), lock held (34), cap stop (33, 35).

findings.title: Commit markers sit at tested points
findings.description: The markers fall after tested, working groups (for example lines 77, 86, 95, 151, 193, 211, 262, 289). None falls after every task or only at the end. The three conditional markers (219, 239, 333) say what to skip when nothing changed.
